newsitem.title: UK: Rowland seeks info on Bock's Lonrho link.
newsitem.headline: Rowland seeks info on Bock's Lonrho link.

text.p: Tiny Rowland, founder of conglomerate Lonrho, said on Friday he had asked for the London Stock Exchange's assistance in finding out whether deputy chairman Dieter Bock still had an interest in Lonrho.
Rowland said he asked the stock exchange to require "full disclosure...by Mr Bock of his arrangements with Anglo American concerning Anglo American's shares in Lonrho".
Bock last month sold all his shares to Anglo American under an option agreement.
But a recent announcement by Lonrho suggested Bock may have retained some interest of which other Lonrho shareholders are unaware, a spokesman for Rowland said.
A Lonrho spokesman responded by saying there were no secret arrangements.

But Rowland said clarity was needed following a statement earlier this week with Bock's official confirmation he sold his Lonrho stake to Anglo American under the option deal agreed in April. Anglo now holds over 25 percent of Lonrho.
But the disclosure also shows there is still an ongoing agreement between Bock and the South African company, the Rowland spokesman said.
"Anglo bought the shares, but Laerstate (a holding company owned by Bock) and Bock have notified the stock exchange that they still have an interest in those shares," the spokesman said.
"That means there is some kind of agreement about it, either a voting agreement or some future interest, but they have not disclosed what the nature of that interest is," he added.
But a Lonrho spokesman dismissed suggestions that Bock still had any voting rights or other links. "That is untrue. All the shares have been sold and that is the end to it," he said.

Bock this year initiated a strategy to split up Lonrho in three after Rowland had been ousted from the board in March 1995 following much-publicised rows with Bock. Lonrho on Friday separately confirmed Bock had stepped down as chief executive to avoid a conflict of interest during the demerger process. Lonrho had already said last month that Bock would become deputy chairman.
The London Stock Exchange, meanwhile, declined to say whether it would ask for any further information from Bock as requested by Rowland.
